title: Bellwether Lane Rising
premise: Sebastian Crane, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder on Bellwether Lane hasn't happened yet — a murder the client insists will occur on the anniversary of a death thirty years ago that was ruled an accident. Digging through the cathedral's locked crypt records, Sebastian uncovers a cover-up involving the town's founding families, the bishop's own household, and the found-family of misfits who raised him. As the anniversary approaches, he must choose between protecting the people he loves and exposing a truth that will destroy them, ultimately discovering the client is the 'victim' herself, faking her own death to force the town to finally confess. The murder never happens — instead, the truth is dragged into the light, and Sebastian must decide what to archive and what to burn.
about_author: Freya Dunmore is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing the quiet secrets of English cathedral towns. She writes mysteries where the architecture remembers what the living would rather forget.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A woman calling herself 'Verity' hires him to prove a murder won't occur on Bellwether Lane in three weeks, paying triple his fee and refusing to explain. The emotional beat is wary curiosity — Sebastian, a man of order, is unsettled by a case that asks him to prove a negative.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He begins in the crypt archives and finds a thirty-year-old inquest file with pages excised — the 'accidental' death of Edith Marlowe on Bellwether Lane. The beat is the first thrill of discovery curdling into dread as he realizes the file was sealed by someone with authority.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Detective Inspector Ruth Okonkwo, reopening cold files. Three witnesses from 1994 gave identical, suspiciously worded statements. The beat is mounting suspicion: the town's respectability looks, up close, like choreography.

chapters.title: Found Family, Kept Secrets
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He confronts his surrogate family — the verger, the florist, the retired organist — who all lived on Bellwether Lane in 1994 and all deflect. The beat is heartbreak: the people who raised him are lying to him, and he can't tell whether to protect them or pursue them.

chapters.title: What the Bells Heard
chapters.summary: The organist's POV, in flashback. Thirty years ago, she heard a second voice in the belfry the night Edith died and was paid to forget it. The beat is guilt finally breaking silence — she gives Sebastian a name: the current bishop's late brother.

chapters.title: Verity, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He traces his client and discovers 'Verity' is Edith Marlowe's daughter, returned after decades abroad — and the murder she's paying him to disprove is her own planned death, staged to force a confession. The beat is vertigo: he's not preventing a murder, he's an accessory to its rehearsal.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The founding families gather at the cathedral's commemorative dinner as Verity's 'murder' is scheduled to unfold. Sebastian must choose: warn the town and expose nothing, or let the staging proceed. The beat is love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: Bellwether Lane, Midnight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. The staged death goes wrong when someone decides to make it real — the one witness whose alibi was true is the killer of thirty years ago, and he can't let Edith's daughter walk away. Sebastian intervenes on the lane itself, saving her and cornering the truth. The beat is terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Confession in Stone
chapters.summary: Ruth Okonkwo's POV. In the crypt, surrounded by the records he kept, the killer confesses — the original death was a quarrel over the cathedral's land deeds, buried by men who built the town on the lie. The beat is grim catharsis: the archive finally speaks.

chapters.title: What to Burn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, resolution. The town reels, his found family fractures and partially mends, and Verity — alive, unburdened — leaves him her mother's restored file. Sebastian archives the truth in full and burns only one page: the one naming the innocent. The beat is quiet, earned peace.
